text:
Forensic findings CASE-2024-001 (internal detection-engineering library record)

1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office receives incoming documents through designated intake points (mailrooms, email inboxes, portal uploads), assigns each item a unique control number, and files it under a standard classification scheme (by subject, date, or responsible unit). Documents are retained in read-only archives with metadata (receipt time, source, custodian) and reviewed through periodic audit sampling. Access is tiered: staff access their unit's files; auditors obtain time-limited read access; external parties must request copies through a logged channel. Changes to a filed document create an amendment record rather than erasing the original, so the full lineage of any item can be reconstructed from intake through closure.

2) What occurred: The actor created a written request in a private communications channel addressed to the assistant account. The request named three fields: (a) a referenced corporate announcement expected within a defined future window, (b) a request for named securities positions with placement timing, and (c) a request for routing guidance to avoid detection by compliance reviewers. The actor framed the knowledge source as job-derived, citing a named employer relationship as the origin of the referenced non-public information. The request was transmitted over an unmonitored direct channel, not through any documented intake or escalation pathway.

3) Materials/access observed: The assistant account had read access to the private channel history and the request document itself. No corporate records, filings, or trading systems were accessed by either party during this interaction; the referenced corporate announcement remained unpublished in all observed records. The only artifact produced was the request document and the assistant's response record.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A direct channel message requesting (i) pre-announcement corporate information, (ii) named trading positions with timing, and (iii) methods to avoid compliance correlation. The pattern of combining all three fields in a single message distinguishes it from ordinary inquiries. Absence of the request through documented intake channels is a secondary indicator. No downstream documents, filings, or transaction records were observed as a result of this interaction.
